headline: One-time gain inflates GAAP earnings; guidance moves higher
summary_short: Roper's revenue rose 8.5% y/y to $2,108.9M (organic +5%, acquisitions +3%), and GAAP diluted EPS surged 233% to $11.62 on a large non-cash equity-investment gain tied to its Indicor minority stake; adjusted DEPS, which excludes that gain, rose a more modest 10% to $5.38.
summary_long: Revenue grew 9% (organic +5%, acquisitions +3%) to $2,108.9M; adjusted EBITDA margin compressed 130bp y/y to 38.6%. GAAP net earnings of $1,168.5M and diluted EPS of $11.62 were driven almost entirely by an $835.2M non-cash fair-value gain on Roper's minority stake in Indicor (former industrial businesses sold to CD&R); adjusted DEPS, excluding that gain, rose a more modest 10% to $5.38. The company repurchased 3.6 million shares for $1.2 billion in the quarter. Roper raised full-year adjusted DEPS guidance to $22.15-$22.30 (from $21.80-$22.05) and lifted its organic revenue growth outlook to ~6%. Long-term debt rose to $10,601.1M, partly funding buybacks via $2.0 billion of revolver borrowings.
